channel.title: Archetype Original: Servant Leadership Devotional
channel.description: A daily devotional on servant leadership by Bart Paden.

item.title: Genuinely Concerned for Your Welfare
item.description: Competence is common and genuine concern for other people is not, which is why who a leader sends says more than who they keep.

item.title: Keeps a Thing Covered
item.description: People calibrate what they tell a leader based on what they have watched that leader repeat.

item.title: They Shall Share Alike
item.description: Visibility and contribution are not the same measure, and only one of them is easy to see.

item.title: When It Is in Your Power
item.description: Having the power to give is what creates the obligation, which removes a leader's usual excuse for waiting.

item.title: Before the Sun Sets
item.description: Holding what is owed is treated as oppression even when nothing is stolen, because the delay costs the one waiting far more than the one holding.

item.title: I Bore the Loss Myself
item.description: A steward who absorbs the losses is doing something different from one who only reports them.

item.title: Rich in Good Works
item.description: Readiness is the test of generosity, because generosity that needs an internal negotiation every time is not ready.

item.title: Wealth Sprouts Wings
item.description: Knowing when to stop acquiring is a skill rather than a loss of nerve, and what is held tightly can still disappear.

item.title: Leave the Edges
item.description: Generosity designed into the harvest does not depend on how a leader feels at the end of a hard year.

item.title: That Nothing May Be Lost
item.description: Abundance reveals whether a leader's care for resources was a value or only a reaction to fear.

item.title: Where There Are No Oxen
item.description: The cost and the capacity are usually the same animal, and a clean manger can mean discipline or avoidance.

item.title: Consider Your Ways
item.description: When output keeps falling short of input, the problem is allocation rather than effort, and leaders usually respond by pushing harder on the same arrangement.

item.title: Know Well the Condition of Your Flocks
item.description: Reported condition and actual condition are different numbers, and the distance between them is where failures grow unnoticed.

item.title: Come Away and Rest a While
item.description: Rest offered in the middle of good work is a different decision than rest granted after someone collapses.

item.title: One Thing Is Necessary
item.description: Good work can crowd out the necessary work, and it almost never feels like a mistake while it is happening.

item.title: Whatever Your Hand Finds to Do
item.description: The reason given for wholehearted work is the closing window, not the worthiness of the assignment.

item.title: Go to the Ant
item.description: Diligence without supervision is the test this proverb sets, for a leader and for the people they lead.

item.title: Plow in the Autumn
item.description: Work with a season attached cannot be recovered by effort later, and most of a leader's most consequential work shows no result on the day it is done.

item.title: A Mist That Appears for a Little Time
item.description: The problem is not the plan but the certainty attached to a future that has not been given yet.

item.title: The Measure of My Days
item.description: Time is the one entrusted resource a leader cannot earn back, which makes asking to feel its limit a practical act rather than a morbid one.

item.title: The Lord Gave
item.description: Stewardship does not remove grief over loss, but it removes the claim that something was stolen.

item.title: He Must Increase
item.description: Influence cannot be seized, only received, which is what makes it possible to rejoice when someone else increases.

item.title: The Might of My Hand
item.description: The story a leader tells about their own success decides what they will do with what they have.

item.title: Strangers and Sojourners
item.description: Every leadership role is temporary, and stewardship includes protecting the future of what a leader holds, not only its present condition.

item.title: Given to the Children of Man
item.description: Real stewardship involves real authority, and what has genuinely been given becomes the responsibility of the one who received it.

item.title: The Earth Is the Lord's
item.description: Every person a leader oversees belonged to God first, which is true even for the founder who built the organization from nothing.

item.title: Work It and Keep It
item.description: Stewardship holds two responsibilities at once, developing what was entrusted and protecting it, and most leaders quietly neglect one of them.

item.title: Mercy Triumphs Over Judgment
item.description: The judgment a leader can expect is tied directly to the mercy they were willing to extend, not abstractly related to it.

item.title: He Delights in Steadfast Love
item.description: Mercy that keeps the offense easily reachable for later isn't the complete mercy this verse describes.

item.title: Blessed Are the Merciful
item.description: Mercy shown and mercy received are described as one connected pattern, not two separate transactions.

item.title: Love Covers a Multitude of Sins
item.description: Covering a multitude of sins is an ongoing posture toward accumulated small failures, not one dramatic act of forgiveness.

item.title: If Your Enemy Is Hungry, Feed Him
item.description: Never avenging yourself is the easier half of this instruction. Actively providing for an enemy is the harder, more specific one.

item.title: Lord, Do Not Hold This Sin Against Them
item.description: Genuine mercy shows up under real pressure. Mercy that only appears when it's comfortable hasn't actually been tested yet.

item.title: Father, Forgive Them
item.description: Forgiveness given with no expectation of it being noticed or received may be the hardest form mercy takes.

item.title: Esau Ran to Meet Him
item.description: Esau extends reconciliation without requiring an apology or confession first.

item.title: Love Your Enemies, Pray for Those Who Persecute You
item.description: Mercy toward someone with no baseline goodwill is where a leader's actual capacity for it gets revealed.

item.title: He Does Not Deal With Us According to Our Sins
item.description: Mercy here is restraint from a fully warranted response, not the absence of grounds for one.

item.title: He Gently Leads Those With Young
item.description: Strength and gentleness are shown as the same character, not competing instincts.

item.title: Bringing Back the One Who Wanders
item.description: Bringing someone back from wandering is an active pursuit, not a passive observation.

item.title: With Complete Patience and Teaching
item.description: Patience is asked to cover the full range from gentle correction to direct rebuke, not just the easier end.

item.title: Those Whom I Love, I Reprove
item.description: Reproof aimed at someone already loved is evidence of an active relationship, not a threat to it.

item.title: Do Not Despise the Lord's Discipline
item.description: Correction from someone who delights in you looks different than correction from someone who merely tolerates you.

item.title: The Lord Disciplines the One He Loves
item.description: Discipline is named as evidence of love in this passage, not a departure from it.

item.title: He Went to Him
item.description: The Samaritan's compassion becomes oil, wine, transportation, and an open account, not just a feeling.

item.title: Charge It to My Account
item.description: Paul asks Philemon to charge a real debt to his own account rather than simply asking for forgiveness.

item.title: The Glory of Overlooking an Offense
item.description: Overlooking an offense is named as glory in this proverb, not weakness.

item.title: While He Was Still a Long Way Off
item.description: Mercy runs out to meet the failure before the apology is finished.

item.title: Kindness for Someone Else's Sake
item.description: David's kindness to Mephibosheth is decided before Mephibosheth ever proves himself.

item.title: Kindness Presumed Upon
item.description: Judging someone for a shared failure and presuming on patience are named as the same posture, not two separate problems.

item.title: A Tender Heart, Put Into Practice
item.description: A tender heart is named as the condition mercy depends on, not something leadership experience should harden away.
